headline: South Chicago and South Shore anchor a ward with the fewest restaurants in the city.
summary:
Ward 7 sits on Chicago's far southeast side, taking in South Deering, South Chicago, South Shore, and Calumet Heights. Only two wards score lower than Ward 7's 48th-place finish. Its combined score sits at 29.04, among the lowest of the fifty.

Commercial life is where the ward struggles most. Ward 7 finishes last in the city, 50th of 50, on restaurants, on food businesses of any kind, and on places still open past 9 p.m. on a weeknight. Commute times are the longest in Chicago too, with about 41 percent of workers on the road 45 minutes or more each way. Rent runs the other direction. Among the 48 wards with reliable rent data, Ward 7 lands 3rd, with a typical asking rent of $1,463, one of the cheapest anywhere in the city. A cluster of pollution-exposure measures also score well for Ward 7, though each comes with its own caveat, covered below.
reading_the_rankings: Start with traffic proximity, where Ward 7 ranks 1st of 50 on the city's Environmental Justice Index. Behind the No. 1 rank sits the same tract-splitting method used across that index. Each census tract's traffic exposure is divided evenly across its acreage and then handed to whichever ward covers that ground, so a tract straddling the Ward 7 line contributes to both sides at once, regardless of where the traffic actually runs. Confidence here again lands at medium, per whoever assembled the index. The restaurant count, dead last at 50th, has a different problem. It is not a ward number at all. It gets built from ZIP code areas, which cut across ward lines however they happen to fall, with no attempt to match the two. This one is rated low confidence too, straight from the people who compiled it. Packaged liquor licenses and food business counts, also dead last, trace back to a ward field the source recorded before the 2023 redraw, so some of what's being measured still reflects the old ward shape rather than today's.

news.headline: Advocate Health Breaks Ground On Hospital At South Chicago Lakefront Megadevelopment Site
news.note: Advocate Health broke ground on a smaller replacement for Trinity Hospital at 8000 S. DuSable Lake Shore Drive, part of a lakefront megadevelopment set to open in 2029.

news.headline: Steel Slag Meets Prairie at Chicago's Marian Byrnes Park, See This Natural Wonder in an Unnatural Setting
news.note: The Chicago Park District added a boardwalk, overlook, and picnic area to the 140-acre natural area in Jeffery Manor, built partly on old steel slag dumping grounds.

news.headline: Artifacts Of Louis Sullivan Building, Demolished In The '50s, Are Protecting South Shore's Lakefront
news.note: Carved limestone remnants of architect Louis Sullivan's demolished Walker Warehouse were found reused as lakefront revetment stone near Rainbow Beach.
